gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads soft and open, its curves stopping short of turning inward so every small letter has room. Against Edo SZ's marker-like line, that gentleness is the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Noto Sans Bassa Vah has a hulking midsection that swallows most of the line, with a c that gapes like pliers. Edo SZ's single-width strokes sit above it, and paragraphs feel sturdy.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-batak: Noto Sans Batak reads big and friendly, its x-height towering like a stubby pencil and its e never squeezed shut. Edo SZ's pencil-like line and that bulk feel companionable.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Low and wide-mouthed, with capitals barely rising above the lowercase. Noto Sans Bengali sits under Edo SZ's single-weight tracing, and a long page would read smoothly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Edo SZ draws its lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, every stroke held to one weight. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki follows with swollen, rope-tight letters and open apertures, so extended text stays easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Edo SZ looks like a bent paperclip, with no thick-thin shifts anywhere. Shrink that heading and its wiry line fades, while Noto Sans Brahmi, with its high mean line and open curves, keeps holding up.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Cast iron stature in a lowercase, drawn with curves that never thin. Noto Sans Buginese does the quieter job, its open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs and short ascenders suiting steady text, while Edo SZ owns the display moments.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid reads spacious, leaving generous room between curve ends and stems beneath a high x-height. Edo SZ draws like a fineliner on paper, while Noto Sans Buhid stays comfortable over a long page.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-carian: Edo SZ stands tall with cast iron stature, its lines holding their thickness throughout. Noto Sans Carian answers with terminals parted like open scissor blades, and the two make a striking contrast between display and sans-serif text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Edo SZ has no hairlines at all, so its stems match everywhere, giving a lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals. Make that heading small and the line thins out, while Noto Sans Chakma's open s and c hold steady.
